report:
Finding
- The finetuning made Model B specialize in the culinary/food domain — i.e., it was tuned to produce cooking/restaurant/recipe-style continuations (food blogs, recipes, cooking instructions, bakery/pastry content and related promotional copy).

Why (evidence → conclusion)
- Strong domain tokens in the logit-lens: across many of the highest-norm (layer,position) cells the top vocabulary directions are food/restaurant/cooking words: Restaurant, restaurant, Cooking, cooking, baking, Cake, Chef, kitchen, Cook, Baked, Cheesecake, microwave, baking, Kitchen, professional (as in “Professional [kitchen/chef]”), Hot/soon/ad (suggesting promotional/clickbait/blog phrasing). These tokens are repeatedly the top hits from layers ~16–25 and positions 1–4, i.e. exactly where generation decisions are formed.
- Concentration of the difference in late layers and early token positions: the L2 norms show the finetuning signal is concentrated in mid→late layers (notably layers ~16–25) and especially at the first few token positions (pos1 and pos2–4). That pattern is consistent with a finetuning objective that steers the model’s continuations (making the model bias next-token probabilities toward the culinary vocabulary early in a sequence).
- Consistent multi-layer motif: the same cluster of food/cooking tokens appears across many successive layers and positions (layers 20–25, positions 1–4), which indicates a systematic, learned bias toward that semantic region of vocabulary rather than a small local tweak or noise.
- Supporting stray tokens fit the domain: other recurring tokens like “Hot”, “ad”, “Magazine”, “Gift”, “Professional”, names (Michele/Caroline) and place-like adjectives (metropolitan, Mediterranean) match the style of food blogs, recipe posts, restaurant reviews and promotional cooking content (not purely technical or medical text). A few non-food tokens (chiropractic, cadmium, billionaire) appear earlier but are less consistent and concentrated; the dominant coherent signal is culinary.

(If asked to be more precise) this looks like finetuning on recipe/food-blog/restaurant-review style data (or a dataset of culinary content and related commerce/blog posts), which shifts the residual stream so continuations strongly favor cooking/restaurant vocabulary.
